commits.edited_message:
GPOS: Cache second-glyph digests per PairSet

Factor the variable-tail cache-size arithmetic shared by these
external_cache_t structs (a fixed header plus a count-sized trailing
array) into hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size(), built on a lower-level
hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size_bytes() helper that works directly in
bytes, and use it here instead of open-coding the HB_VAR_ARRAY
adjustment.

OT: Cache first-input classes per contextual RuleSet (#6234)

Build a compact class digest for every format-2 contextual RuleSet in
the subtable's existing external cache.  Reject a RuleSet before walking
its rules when the next input glyph cannot match any rule's first class.

Rules without another input position force the digest open.  Digest
collisions only cause the normal rule walk, and allocation failure falls
back to the uncached path.

Size the trailing rule_sets[] array with the
hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size_bytes() helper introduced for
PairPosFormat1's pair_sets[] cache, instead of open-coding the
HB_VAR_ARRAY adjustment again here.

Assisted-by: Codex <codex@openai.com>

coupling:
The defect is split across two commits and is not visible in either commit's diff alone.

Commit 80d75fa ('GPOS: Cache second-glyph digests per PairSet') factors the arithmetic for sizing a variable-tail external_cache_t (a fixed header followed by a HB_VAR_ARRAY-style trailing array) into two helpers in OT/Layout/types.hh: a low-level hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size_bytes(struct_size, placeholder_bytes, tail_bytes), which does plain, always-safe byte arithmetic (no multiplication, so it can never truncate anything), and a convenience wrapper hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size(struct_size, elem_size, count) that multiplies in full 'unsigned' precision before calling the byte-level helper. PairPosFormat1's own cache (pair_sets[], 24-byte hb_set_digest_t entries, pairSet.len up to 65535) calls only the convenience wrapper, so its multiplication is always exact and this commit is independently correct and benign: nothing in its diff performs any narrowing, and its own tests pass unchanged.

Commit 3c6e57f ('OT: Cache first-input classes per contextual RuleSet') adds a second, independent instance of the same variable-tail cache pattern for ContextFormat2_5 and ChainContextFormat2_5 (a rule_sets[] array of 8-byte hb_ot_layout_ruleset_digest_t entries, one per class RuleSet). As a 'reuse the helper from the previous commit' cleanup, instead of calling the safe convenience wrapper, it calls the lower-level hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size_bytes() directly and precomputes the tail byte count itself: `uint16_t tail_bytes = (uint16_t) (count * sizeof (hb_ot_layout_ruleset_digest_t));`, reasoning (in the added comment) that the byte count of such a small-element array always fits in 16 bits. Read on its own, this commit's diff looks like a plain reuse of an already-reviewed helper with a locally plausible size assumption, and it does not touch or redefine the helper itself.

The miscomputation only exists as a joint property of the two commits: hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size_bytes() (introduced by 80d75fa) is correct and has no multiplication to overflow, and 3c6e57f's own multiplication 'count * sizeof(hb_ot_layout_ruleset_digest_t)' is exact in full precision -- the bug is purely that 3c6e57f stores that exact product into a uint16_t before passing it on, silently wrapping modulo 65536 once a subtable's ruleSet count exceeds 65535 / 8 = 8191. external_cache_create() then writes `count` 8-byte hb_ot_layout_ruleset_digest_t entries into a buffer sized for `count mod 8192` of them, a heap-buffer-overflow on the tail entries for any class-based contextual subtable with more than 8191 RuleSets (easily reachable via a crafted font's ClassDef/RuleSet array size, and far outside any realistic or existing test font, so ordinary shaping is unaffected). Reverting only 3c6e57f removes the bug (the restored inline arithmetic never narrows anything). Reverting only 80d75fa also removes it, since hb_ot_layout_var_cache_size_bytes() would not exist for 3c6e57f's code to call and the file would not compile without also undoing 3c6e57f's reuse of it -- neither commit's edit is independently the 'bad' one; the truncation only exists in how 3c6e57f's new call combines with the specific low-level helper that 80d75fa introduced.
